14213: Campground beside the Little Muskegon River near Morley, with something going on every weekend: kids' crafts, games, theme weekends, cornhole, dance parties and karaoke.  A swimming pool opens from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend, and there is a jump pad, mini-golf, a basketball court, a game room and rec room, and a large picnic area by the river.  It has an LP fill station and delivers firewood and ice to the site, and bikers on the White Pine Bike Trail get special rustic rates Sunday to Thursday.  Cabins and park models are rented. --Claude
14214: Campground in natural woods along Duke Creek, an official trout stream (fishing needs a license), 18 miles north of Grand Rapids in Cedar Springs.  Every weekend brings arts and crafts, an activity, a penny dive and a wagon ride, and there are hiking trails and a pool with no lifeguard on duty.  Sites have a fire ring and a picnic table but no grill.  Aggressive dog breeds aren't allowed, nor is outside firewood.  Cabins and park models are also rented. --Claude
14220: Family-owned campground, celebrating 42 seasons, in the wooded dunes 2 miles north of Pentwater, with gated entrances.  AJ's Family Fun Center, inside the campground, has go-karts, mini-golf, an arcade and ice cream.  There are two heated pools (no lifeguard), volleyball, tetherball, ping-pong, hiking, disc golf and a fish-cleaning station, and mobile pump-outs come on Mondays and Fridays.  Log cabins sleep five, and golf carts, ATVs and UTVs aren't allowed in the campground. --Claude
14221: RV park in the Manistee National Forest at Wellston, with the Whitetail Party Mart at its entrance, Fawn Crest Golf Course a short walk away, Tippy Dam 3 miles off and Lake Michigan 17 miles west on M-55.  A food truck comes Wednesday to Sunday, and there is a community fire pit, pollinator gardens and digital detox zones, with lighting kept low after 10 p.m.  Its 20-amp sites suit smaller trailers, camper vans, truck campers and pop-ups, there are rustic non-electric sites, and a cottage, a retro trailer and a glamping tent are rented.  The person booking must be 21, seasonal campers go through a background check, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude
14222: Franchise Jellystone Park in the woods outside Grayling.  A site may share its water and electric pedestal with another, so extension cords and extra hoses may be needed, and sewer sites are limited.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a jumping pillow, mini golf, a Silent Disco (new in 2026) and a Bear Factory; day passes cost $15 a person, Sunday to Thursday, and early check-in $35.  The person booking must be 21 and a site holds one immediate family; e-bikes, EV charging and outside firewood aren't allowed, nor are golf carts for overnight guests.  Two dogs at most; quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m.  Cabins and RVs are rented. --Claude
14223: Campground, family-owned since 1977, on over 50 wooded acres beside Brush Creek in Lawrence, just south of I-94 at Exit 52.  There are hiking trails, a playground and fishing; firewood costs $7 a bundle and visitors $5 each.  Generators, fireworks and chainsaws aren't allowed, golf carts, ATVs and UTVs need permission, and quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude
14224: Campground in an oak grove with private hiking trails near Montague.  Its grass-and-dirt sites take RVs or tents, and there is frisbee golf, horseshoes and cornhole.  A honeywagon is an optional add-on, and seasonal sites are booked by calling or emailing. --Claude
14226: Family campground five miles southwest of downtown Gaylord, near Otsego Lake and thousands of acres of state forest.  It has an indoor pool and spa, an outdoor waterslide, a playground, a stocked trout lake for fishing and an 18-hole mini golf course, plus basketball, horseshoes, kayak rentals and an arcade; a fitness center is being developed.  There are picnic areas and fire pits, cabins and campers are rented, and there is an event venue. --Claude
14227: Campground near Houghton Lake, Michigan's largest inland lake by surface area, with large wooded sites.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a fishing pond, basketball, volleyball, horseshoes, a large open playground and a dog run; propane is sold, firewood is delivered to the site, and ORV trails are nearby.  Cabins and a bunk house are rented, there are seasonal sites, and monthly camping is offered after Labor Day.  Outside firewood isn't allowed, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude
14228: Campground in rolling hills near Marcellus, with fishing, hiking and walking trails, a pool and a playground.  RV sites have full hookups on gravel, or water, electric and greywater, with the black tank dumped at the end of the stay; power is a 110-volt plug on a 30-amp breaker, so adapters may be needed.  The Olive Branch camper and the Mustard Seed cabin are rented, there is a primitive tent site, and an extra vehicle costs $5 a day. --Claude
14229: Christian non-profit camp near Hastings that rents campsites and cabins by the day or week alongside its camps and retreats for youth, adults and families.  It has an outdoor pool (Memorial Day to Labor Day), gaga ball pits, basketball, volleyball, tetherball, a playground, a 9-hole frisbee golf course and a nature trail; firewood is $5 a bundle, and seasonal sites cost $1,200 a year.  Tobacco, alcohol and illegal drugs aren't allowed, campers are expected to dress modestly, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude
14234: Family campground on Turner Lake, a natural 18-acre lake with a sandy beach (no lifeguard), bordered by state land and close to Deep Lake, Gun Lake and the Yankee Springs Recreation Area.  Some sites are lakeside.  Kayaks, canoes, rowboats and paddleboards rent for $5 an hour on site or $20 an hour off site, and paddleboats for $10 for the first hour and $5 for each hour after; there are hiking trails and a fenced dog park.  Annual events include bingo, crafts, a kayak race, cornhole and fishing tournaments and live music; ice costs $4 a bag and firewood $6 a bundle, which can be delivered to the site.  Golf carts are allowed with a licensed driver 16 or older and insurance, and cabins are rented. --Claude
14235: RV park on 40 wooded acres of pines near Manton, a base for day trips to Traverse City, Frankfort, Lake City, Cadillac and Sleeping Bear Dunes.  There is a walking trail, a playground and sandbox, fowling and a covered pavilion for events. --Claude
14250: Fishing campground and cabin retreat on 22 wooded acres at Diana, a short drive from Webster Springs, where a creek and a river line two sides of the property.  RV sites #4-10 are on a tree-lined creekside lane; sites are level back-ins on gravel and grass, each with a fire ring, and picnic tables are available on request, first come, first served.  Pete's Pond, three acres and stocked, has daily fishing and monthly tournaments, and there are canoes, kayaks, a paddle boat, swimming holes and a hiking trail.  Riverside tent sites, cabins and glamping are also offered, and a small grocery and a diner are down the street.  Pets are allowed for a fee; generators aren't. --Claude
14251: Locally owned campground on the outskirts of Belington, near Audra State Park and a little under 2 miles from the Middle Fork River, with a catch-and-release fishing pond on site (no license needed, no swimming).  There are hiking trails, a small playground and the Grand Pavilion, new in 2025 with a custom fireplace and stonework; firewood is delivered to the site, and the major carriers have cell service.  Generators, ATVs, UTVs and golf carts aren't allowed, and a site may have three dogs at most. --Claude
14375: Newly established RV park surrounded by nature in Dublin, minutes from shopping, designed for long-term stays but offering overnight and seasonal sites.  Sites have spacious gravel pads, and pets are welcome. --Claude
14446: RV park at Robertsdale with a clubhouse and special events.  Children are allowed for single-night stays, not by the week or month. --Claude
14521: Campground at Fullerton, beneath towering shade trees near the Cedar River.  Overnight guests have river access for fishing and swimming, and the campground runs floats down the Cedar River by reservation: a stock tank for up to 4 people is $100 for 3½ hours, a tube $25 and a kayak $30.  There are jeep trails (open as conditions allow), hiking trails, a playground and summer concerts; portable toilets stand on site, and sites have picnic tables and fire rings.  Cottages and monthly sites are also offered. --Claude
14553: Family resort on twenty-seven acres near Joplin, by Shoal Creek and a natural spring, with a restaurant on site.  Campers can fish in Shoal Creek and bring their own kayaks (there are no rentals, and self-shuttling costs $5 a car), and tent island, between the creek and the spring, is reached by footbridge.  Beach cabanas ($99 a night) and wagon lodging ($199) are rented, propane, wood and ice are sold, and a tank pump-out costs $10.  A day pass costs $5 a car, and a site may have two pets at most. --Claude
